reasoning: Read test/test_ducklib.py:1634-1647 (test_create_array_value): it creates a 3-element ARRAY value via duckdb_create_array_value, asserts only `av != 0` (line 1641), then destroys it. No size or element-content check is performed. This is directly comparable to the sibling container tests in the same file -- test_create_get_list_value (1531-1548), test_create_get_map_value (1563-1596), and test_create_get_struct_value (1600-1633) -- all of which read children back via duckdb_get_list_child/duckdb_get_map_key/duckdb_get_map_value/duckdb_get_struct_child and assert the underlying int32 values. The array test has no analogous readback, so a duckdb_create_array_value binding that produced an empty or garbage-but-non-null value would still pass. Verified against numbduck/ducklib.py:450-453 (duckdb_create_array_value wrapper) and confirmed via DuckDB's actual C API source (src/main/capi/duckdb_value-c.cpp) that duckdb_get_list_child/duckdb_get_list_size explicitly check `val.type().id() != LogicalTypeId::LIST` and reject ARRAY-typed values (return nullptr/0) -- so the finding's suggested fix wording ('list-child accessors on the value') is technically imprecise (list-child does NOT work on ARRAY values), but this only affects the recommendation, not the core defect: the test genuinely never reads back size or contents, and no other test in the suite exercises an ARRAY value's contents (grep for 'array'/'ARRAY' across test/ shows only this one test plus unrelated logical-type-metadata tests at lines 1797-1800). A viable fix does exist despite the imprecise recommendation, e.g. duckdb_value_to_string(av) on the array value (already bound and used elsewhere, e.g. test_value_to_string) would render '[1, 2, 3]' and validate contents, or a DB round-trip like the sibling test_list_value_from_column_logical_type (1650+) using an ARRAY column. The defect is real and correctly characterized (too-loose assertion, genuine coverage gap in the array-value path); severity 'low' is appropriate since this is a test-quality gap in a single value-creation helper, not a production code correctness bug, and matches the severity assigned to the directly analogous sibling finding TST-COR-1.
notes_recommendation_caveat: Reviewer's proposed fix mechanism (list-child accessors on the value) is factually wrong per DuckDB's C API (LIST-only check); a correct fix would use duckdb_value_to_string or a DB round-trip instead. This does not change the verdict on the core finding.
